httpsHelp.androidSteps: Android: Copy the .crt file to the phone. Then Settings → Security → Encryption & credentials → Install a certificate → CA certificate. Names differ between manufacturers; searching the settings for “certificate” helps. Android then shows a notice that the network may be monitored. With your own certificate, that’s normal.
httpsHelp.cautionText: Only install certificates you created yourself. Whoever controls an installed root certificate can read the encrypted connections of apps that trust it.
httpsHelp.domain: Your own or a free domain (e.g. DuckDNS) with a reverse proxy such as Caddy, which gets a Let’s Encrypt certificate automatically.
httpsHelp.iosSteps: iPhone: Open the .crt file, e.g. via AirDrop or email. Then Settings → Profile Downloaded → Install. Afterwards, turn on full trust for the certificate under Settings → General → About → Certificate Trust Settings.
httpsHelp.ownCertificate: Without a domain: your own certificate
httpsHelp.ownCertificateText: Create your own certificate for the server’s address, for example with Caddy (“tls internal”) or mkcert. It must be valid for exactly the address you enter in Unterwegs (name or IP). Then install the root certificate (CA) on the phone, not the server certificate.
httpsHelp.tailscale: Tailscale: “tailscale serve” makes the server reachable at https://<name>.ts.net for all devices in your tailnet.
httpsHelp.thenSignIn: Then enter the address with https:// in Unterwegs.
httpsHelp.title: Setting up HTTPS
httpsHelp.whyText: Unterwegs sends your API key with every request. Over http://, anyone on the same Wi-Fi could read it. That’s why the app only connects over https://.
httpsHelp.withName: Easiest: an address with a certificate
httpsHelp.withNameText: Give the server an address with a valid certificate. Then there’s nothing to install on the phone. For example:
